how_read: Pages read with scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py (--api https://www.mariowiki.com/api.php --titles ...). The wiki refused the reader's by-revision render call, and the reader fell back by itself to asking for the page by title, checking that the revision it rendered is the revision it had looked up; the revision below is the one the reader printed for each page. Every quoted fragment was checked, by script, to occur word for word in the fetched page text (whitespace collapsed). The pages are kept in build/wiki-live/mariowiki/ in the helper's copy. Where a page covers the whole series, a line uses only what the page says about Yoshi's Story.

lines.line: Summary: The boss waiting at the end of the level Frustration. He stomps from one side of the room to the other, and pots and pans drop from above while he does.

quoted: In Yoshi's Story, Don Bongo is fought at the end of Stage 3-4: Frustration. He attacks by stomping back and forth across the room, causing pots and pans to rain down from the ceiling.

lines.line: Weak points: Three hits on his lips with eggs beat him. An egg that lands anywhere else on him just bounces off.

quoted: a Baby Yoshi has to hit him in the lips three times; hitting him anywhere else simply causes the egg to bounce off his blubber.

lines.line: Looks like: A chubby creature like a dragon, green and spotted with yellow, with thick red lips and a striped yellow stomach.

quoted: He is a pudgy dragon-like creature with green skin, yellow spots, big red lips, a yellow stomach with stripes, and a big orange-and-yellow belly button.

lines.line: Tips: Bumping into him is harmless, since you simply bounce away. What drops from the ceiling is the only danger.

quoted: The Baby Yoshi does not lose any health if he touches Don Bongo, simply bouncing off him instead. Only the items falling from the ceiling can hurt the Baby Yoshi.

lines.line: Tips: His lips puff up after every hit, making them somewhat easier to aim at, but after the second hit he speeds up a lot.

quoted: After each hit, Don Bongo's lips swell, making them a somewhat easier target, although his movement becomes a lot faster after his lips are hit twice.

lines.line: Summary: A genie made of smoke that you face once the level Poochy & Nippy has its 30 fruits eaten. He sends spiked balls rolling down slippery see-saws and breathes fire.

quoted: He is a smoke djinn that was sent by Baby Bowser to patrol the mountains of Yoshi's Island in Yoshi's Story. As such, a Yoshi must fight him after collecting 30 fruits in Stage 3-3: Poochy & Nippy. He attacks by using large spiked balls and causes them to roll down slippery teeter-totters, and breathes fire at the Yoshi.

lines.line: Weak points: Three eggs thrown at his stomach beat him, and only while he is tangible.

quoted: Hitting his stomach with three eggs (while he is tangible) defeats him.
A Yoshi's egg can harm Cloudjin while he is tangible

lines.line: Looks like: A giant genie made of smoke that floats about.

quoted: A giant, wind-bending genie that floats around.
He is a smoke djinn

lines.line: Tips: He flashes red when an egg hurts him, but only in the Japanese release; the international releases do not show it.

quoted: Cloudjin flashes red when hurt in the Japanese version only.
causing him to flash red (though not in international releases).

lines.line: Summary: A ghost boss met last in The Tall Tower. He turns invisible and tries to run into Yoshi while summoning Peepers.

quoted: He is at the end of The Tall Tower.
Inviso attacks by turning invisible and trying to bump into a Yoshi while summoning Peepers.
A ghost that remains invisible while releasing Peepers to attack.

lines.line: Weak points: It takes three egg hits to beat him.

quoted: The Yoshi can defeat Inviso by hitting him with three eggs.

lines.line: Looks like: He is invisible; the only thing that shows is the world reflected on him.

quoted: Inviso's appearance is somewhat hidden, as he is invisible (minus the fact that the world reflects on him).

lines.line: Tips: An egg that strips a Peeper of its feathers makes it fall, and eating it at that point heals Yoshi fully.

quoted: When a Peeper is shot down, a puff of smoke appears, and the Peeper loses its feathers and falls away. If a Yoshi eats a Peeper when it loses its feathers, it will heal him back to full health.
In addition, Inviso summons Peepers during his boss battle.
If a Yoshi shoots one with an egg, it will lose its feathers and fall down.

lines.line: Summary: The boss at the end of the level Cloud Cruising, a smiling cloud made of cotton candy.

quoted: fought at the end of Cloud Cruising. She is a colossal, buoyant, smiling cloud composed of fluffy yellow cotton candy.

lines.line: Weak points: You beat her by licking her. Each lick takes a piece off her, so she shrinks, and she is beaten once all of her has been eaten.

quoted: In order to defeat Cloud N. Candy, a Yoshi has to lick her, which will pick off pieces of her, causing her to shrink until she is fully eaten.

lines.line: Looks like: An enormous, floating cloud with a smile, fluffy and yellow, made of cotton candy.

quoted: She is a colossal, buoyant, smiling cloud composed of fluffy yellow cotton candy.

lines.line: Tips: She hops about during the fight and hurts you on contact. The smaller she gets, the quicker and more agile she becomes. Licking her also gives back some of your health.

quoted: Cloud N. Candy jumps during the fight, damaging the player if they touch her, and as she gets smaller, she becomes quicker and more agile. Each time she is licked, the player will recover some health.

lines.line: Summary: Hydra-like skeleton dragons that usually bar your way in the level Bone Dragon Pit and sometimes spit a fireball.

quoted: Bone Dragons are large hydra-like dragon skeletons that Yoshis encounter in the Bone Dragon Pit in Yoshi's Story. Bone Dragons usually block a Yoshi's way
they can attack the Yoshis by occasionally spitting a fireball at them.

lines.line: Weak points: Two hits to the head, from eggs or from a ground pound, get you past one. On a three-headed one, each head takes two hits of its own.

quoted: to get past one, the Yoshi has to either throw eggs at its head or ground-pound it, with either method taking two hits to defeat the Bone Dragon.
Each of the heads takes two hits

lines.line: Looks like: A large dragon skeleton that looks like a hydra. In a couple of places you meet a three-headed one that has a body as well.

quoted: large hydra-like dragon skeletons
a Yoshi encounters a three-headed Bone Dragon, complete with a body.

lines.line: Tips: Touching the body of a three-headed one does not hurt you. Beating a Bone Dragon earns three melons.

quoted: Touching the body does not hurt the Yoshi.
defeating the Bone Dragon earns the Yoshi three melons.

lines.line: Summary: A serpentine enemy in just one area of Lots O'Jelly Fish, a level, that circles around a Yoshi it spots swimming nearby. It counts as a mini-boss, yet it cannot be defeated.

quoted: is a serpentine enemy that appears in Yoshi's Story.

it is found in a single area of the level Lots O'Jelly Fish, where it waits for a Yoshi to swim nearby. When it spots them, it swims in circles around them, attempting to enclose them within its spiky body
Despite being treated as a mini-boss, it cannot be defeated

lines.line: Looks like: A big, white, green-spiked creature whose tail is one large fin. Its head is a round ball with red eyes and flippers, and a spout where a mouth would be.

quoted: It resembles a large white creature with green spikes and a large fin for a tail. Its head is a large ball with red eyes, flippers, and a spout for a mouth.

lines.line: Tips: Eggs cannot be thrown while you are underwater, which makes it as good as invincible. What you have to do is defeat the Cheep Cheeps inside its lair while avoiding it.

quoted: since Yoshis cannot throw eggs underwater, the Snorkel Snake is effectively invincible.
the Cheep Cheeps in its lair must be defeated while the Yoshi avoids it.

lines.line: Tips: Its body is too short to close a full circle, so a Yoshi it has ringed can still swim out.

quoted: its body is not long enough for it to make a complete circle, allowing the Yoshis to escape if encircled.

lines.line: Summary: A fruit that turns the Yoshi who eats it Super Happy, but only for a limited time. Some are found in bubbles, and one drifts down from the sky when you eat six matching fruits back to back.

quoted: Heart Fruits can be found in bubbles; alternatively, when a Yoshi eats six of the same fruit in a row, a Heart Fruit appears from the sky and slowly floats down.
It is activated whenever a Yoshi eats a Heart Fruit.
Super Happy Yoshi lasts for only a limited time

lines.line: Uses: Super Happy makes a Yoshi invincible and stronger, gives unlimited eggs, a longer tongue and a better flutter jump, and fills the Smile Meter completely. Ground-pounding in this form bursts every bubble on the screen, and peppers become coins while Shy Guys become Lucky Fruit.

quoted: Super Happy Yoshi is invincible and stronger and has a longer tongue, an infinite supply of eggs, and a better Flutter Jump.
If Super Happy Yoshi performs a ground pound, he pops all bubbles onscreen, Shy Guys turn into the current Lucky Fruit, and peppers turn into coins.
While a Yoshi is Super Happy, the Smile Meter, which represents the Yoshi's health, laughs and is completely filled.

lines.line: Tips: The form wears off at once if you eat anything such as a pepper, a blue Tehee Butterfly or a Black Shy Guy, or if a Piranha Pest eats you. Entering a new area that turns the page also ends it.

quoted: its effects wear off immediately if a Yoshi eats anything like a blue Tehee Butterfly, a Black Shy Guy, or a pepper or if a Yoshi is eaten by a Piranha Pest.
Moving to a new area that causes the page to turn also ends the effect early.

lines.line: Tips: Even Super Happy invincibility cannot save you from fatal hazards like pits, lava, pistons and Blurps.

quoted: Lastly, the form's invincibility does not protect the Yoshi from fatal hazards, such as Blurps, pits, lava, and pistons.

lines.line: Summary: Three Special Hearts are hidden in every level, and each one you pick up unlocks a level on the following page.

quoted: Each stage has three Special Hearts hidden throughout the stage.
Each Special Heart opens a new level on the next page

lines.line: Uses: From the second page onward, the following page lets you in only to its opening level, unless you collected a Special Heart in the level you just played. Collecting all three is what unlocks every level of the following page. Picking one up also restores a Yoshi's health completely.

quoted: only the first level of the next page can be accessed unless a Special Heart is collected in the current level; this applies to all pages past the first page.
meaning that all three Special Hearts are needed to unlock all the levels on the next page.
Unlocks a level on the next page; fully heals a Yoshi

lines.line: Tips: You hear chimes as a Baby Yoshi gets near one. Throwing an egg at one also collects it.

quoted: Ringing chimes sound when a Baby Yoshi is close to a Special Heart.
Eggs can also be thrown to collect coins and Special Hearts.

lines.line: Tips: Each Special Heart is worth 100 hearts. Collecting them also boosts Yoshi's Mood when the stage ends.

quoted: Special Hearts also boost Yoshi's Mood at the end of a stage
Special Hearts are worth 100 hearts.

lines.line: Summary: A special sunflower that grows out of the ground. A Baby Yoshi can eat its head to recover.

quoted: A Power Flower is a special sunflower that appears in Yoshi's Story. It grows from the ground
The head of a Power Flower can be consumed by a Baby Yoshi

lines.line: Uses: The head restores two petals on the Smile Meter. Unlike fruit and Shy Guys it scores no points, so it does not raise Yoshi's Mood once the stage is finished.

quoted: This allows him to recover two petals on his Smile Meter, but it does not earn him any points, unlike eating a fruit or a Shy Guy, and thus does not improve Yoshi's Mood when the stage is completed.

lines.line: Looks like: A sunflower with a green stem and leaves. Its head is yellow, with a small red mouth, black eyes and red petals.

quoted: has a green stem with green leaves, as well as a yellow head with red petals, black eyes, and a small red mouth.

lines.line: Tips: The head regrows fast once eaten, so you can keep nibbling heads until your health is completely back.

quoted: The head of the Power Flower quickly regrows after being consumed, meaning that the Yoshi can simply keep eating flower heads until his health is fully recovered.

lines.line: Summary: A spiky fruit found only in the level Jungle Puddle. Most Yoshis find the taste awful.

quoted: Bomb Berries appear only in Jungle Puddle.
An explosive spiked fruit that tastes horrible to Yoshis (except the Black and White Yoshis).

lines.line: Uses: Contact with one costs the Yoshi some petals of the Smile Meter. Eating one also costs petals, though the Black and White Yoshis are spared.

quoted: Getting in contact with a Bomb Berry causes a Yoshi to make its Smile Meter lose some petals. Eating it also causes the Yoshi to lose petals (except for the Black and White Yoshis).

lines.line: Looks like: Shaped like an eggplant, in yellow and red, and covered in green spikes.

quoted: Bomb Berries resemble yellow-and-red eggplants and are covered in green spikes.

lines.line: Tips: You cannot see a Bomb Berry at first. Once you walk by, it starts growing to its full size, and it keeps growing until its own weight makes it drop into the water and slowly sink. After a while a new berry grows at the same spot.

quoted: At first, they are invisible, but once the player walks past them, they begin to grow to full size. They continue to grow until their weight causes them to fall off into the water, where they slowly sink to the bottom. A new Bomb Berry then grows from the original spot after a while.

lines.line: Summary: An elephant-like creature that bars the way with a stop sign. Three of them stand in the level Treasure Hunt, and nowhere else.

quoted: Pak E. Derms are elephant-like creatures that first appear in Yoshi's Story. They can always be seen carrying a stop sign with which they do not allow the Yoshis to pass.
Yoshi encounters three Pak E. Derms in only one level—the P. 1-Beginning level Treasure Hunt.

lines.line: Tips: Ground-pound the floor and it tips onto its head, letting you through. Move fast: it soon gets back on its feet.

quoted: To pass, Yoshi has to Ground Pound the ground, and the Pak E. Derm will fall on his head, allowing Yoshi to pass. Yoshi has to act quickly because Pak E. Derm will soon flip back upright.

lines.line: Tips: It stands on whichever path you have chosen, and shifts across to the other one if you change paths.

quoted: Pak E. Derms stand in the middle of the path Yoshi is taking, and will move to the other path if Yoshi moves to the other path.

lines.line: Summary: A flying butterfly that keeps changing colour between pink and blue. What happens when you eat it depends on its colour at that moment.

quoted: They fly around and change color from pink to blue. Eating a pink one restores a Yoshi's health, but eating a blue one depletes it due to bitterness
A butterfly that flashes between pink and blue.

lines.line: Looks like: A round flying insect that changes colour from pink to blue.

quoted: are flying spherical insects
change color from pink to blue

lines.line: Tips: A pink one restores health when eaten, while a blue one tastes bitter and drains it. Eating a blue one while Super Happy cuts that form short.

quoted: Eating a pink one restores a Yoshi's health, but eating a blue one depletes it due to bitterness
If a Yoshi eats a blue Tehee Butterfly while Super Happy, the Super Happy effect ends early.

lines.line: Tips: When you bounce off one as a springboard, the wiki calls it a Tehee Trampoline.

quoted: also called Tehee Trampolines in the context of jumping on them as springboards

lines.line: Summary: An aggressive kind of Flying Shy Guy, first met in the level Poochy & Nippy.

quoted: Black Shy Guys are an aggressive type of Flying Shy Guy found in Yoshi's Story.
These Shy Guys first appear in Poochy & Nippy.

lines.line: Tips: In Poochy & Nippy they dive in from the top of the screen and drop bombs on you, and you can use those bombs to smash rock blocks. On Page 6 they hang in the air carrying weights meant to fall on whoever passes beneath, and a ground pound near one makes it let go at once.

quoted: In this level, the Black Shy Guys swoop down from above the screen, dropping bombs on top of the Yoshis. This can be used to the Yoshis' advantage by causing them to break rock blocks. Black Shy Guys also appear on Page 6, hovering about in the air, holding weights to drop on Yoshis that pass underneath them. They automatically drop them if a Yoshi ground-pounds near one.

lines.line: Tips: Unlike an ordinary Flying Shy Guy, a ground pound near one has no effect on it. Eating one yields a black-spotted egg, but most Yoshis show disgust and lose three Smile Meter petals, and the Super Happy form ends. Black and White Yoshis appear able to stomach it and gain two petals.

quoted: Unlike with normal Flying Shy Guys, performing a Ground Pound near them does not affect them in any way.

after eating one, they look disgusted and lose three petals from their Smile Meter. Eating a Black Shy Guy also nullifies the Super Happy form. Black and White Yoshis seem to be able to tolerate Black Shy Guys and gain two petals. When a Black Shy Guy is eaten, it turns into an egg with black spots.

lines.line: Summary: A giant pink balloon that waits inside a Mystery Crate. You find them only in the back half of Surprise!!, a level on Page 1.

quoted: are giant pink balloon enemies that reside in Mystery Crates in Yoshi's Story.
Exclusively found in the second half of the Page 1 level Surprise!!

lines.line: Weak points: Hit the bandages stuck on its belly twice, with eggs or with Huffin Puffin's chicks. When it goes down it deflates and vanishes, leaving a melon.

quoted: To defeat an Air Bag, the Yoshi must throw an egg or one of Huffin Puffin's chicks at the pair of bandages on its belly twice. Upon defeat, the bandages fall off and the Air Bag deflates until it disappears, leaving a melon.

lines.line: Looks like: A huge pink balloon with two bandages on its belly.

quoted: are giant pink balloon enemies
the pair of bandages on its belly

lines.line: Tips: You can neither shove the crate nor smash it with a ground pound. Firing an egg or a chick at the crate reveals the Air Bag inside.

quoted: Mystery Crates that the Baby Yoshis cannot push or destroy via ground-pounding. Air Bags can be revealed by shooting an egg or one of Huffin Puffin's chicks at the crates.

lines.line: Tips: It attacks by blowing a powerful blast of wind at you. That does no damage, but it may knock you into other enemies.

quoted: Air Bags attack by blowing a strong gust of air at a Yoshi that deals no damage, but it can risk pushing them into enemies.

lines.line: Summary: A blindfolded Boo that homes in on sounds, since it cannot see. Four of them haunt the Ghost Castle and nowhere else, three early on and one during the tower climb.

quoted: Since it cannot see, a Blindfold Boo relies on sound to guide it. When it hears a sound, such as a Yoshi gathering coins, it homes in on the sound.
Blindfold Boos appear only in the Ghost Castle, where four of them (three in the beginning and one in the tower climb)

lines.line: Looks like: In this game it has a light-blue blindfold, not a black one, and fake pink ears instead of arms.

quoted: In Yoshi's Story, Blindfold Boos were redesigned to have light-blue blindfolds, rather than black, and have fake pink ears rather than arms.

lines.line: Tips: Attacks do nothing to it, and while it chases you it can outrun a Yoshi. Touching it, or being hit by any attack of its, costs three Smile Meter petals.

quoted: they are invulnerable to attacks, and when pursuing a Yoshi, they can move faster than a Yoshi can run. If a Yoshi touches a Blindfold Boo or receives any attack by one, he loses three petals from the Smile Meter.
